message.content:
In a standard poker hand the “hearts” you’re counting are just the cards of the hearts suit.  
So the maximum number of hearts a single player can hold in a hand is:

| Game | Cards considered for the best hand | Max hearts a player can have |
|------|------------------------------------|------------------------------|
| 5‑card poker (e.g., Five‑Card Draw) | 5 cards | **5** hearts (a hearts flush) |
| Texas Hold’em | 5 cards chosen from 7 (2 hole + 5 community) | **5** hearts (the best 5‑card hand) |
| Texas Hold’em (all 7 cards) | 7 cards | **7** hearts (if you look at all 7 cards, not just the best 5) |

So, in the usual sense of “best hand,” the highest number of hearts a player can have is **five**. If you count all seven cards in Texas Hold’em, a player could technically hold up to **seven** hearts, but only five of those would be used to form the best hand.
